rcw-36.name: RCW 36 Emission Nebula
rcw-36.coordinate_notes: Coordinates RA 134.8708°, DEC -43.7533° (08h 59m 29s, -43° 45′ 12″) represent the project-selected IRSA SIA2 query center matching the Explorer sky tile and yielding 70 SPHEREx QR3 observation records. The SIMBAD catalog reference position for the central ionizing cluster of Gum 20 / RCW 36 is RA 134.7538°, DEC -43.7361° (08h 59m 00.9s, -43° 44′ 10″).

query_center.purpose: SPHEREx QR3 SIA2 archive search center (70 observation records)

rcw-36.description: A compact star-forming H II emission nebula situated within Cloud C of the Vela Molecular Ridge. Ionized by massive embedded O/B stars and observed by SPHEREx across 96 infrared spectral channels.

hotspots.name: Embedded Stellar Cluster
hotspots.fact: Contains over 350 young stellar objects and protostars ionizing surrounding molecular gas.

hotspots.name: Bipolar Molecular Outflow
hotspots.fact: Dense molecular gas cavity carved out by stellar winds from central massive stars.

rcw-36.source: NASA ADS / SIMBAD Gum 20 / IPAC IRSA SPHEREx QR3 Catalog

vela-ridge.name: Vela Molecular Ridge
vela-ridge.coordinate_notes: Coordinates RA 133.7500°, DEC -44.0000° (08h 55m 00s, -44° 00′ 00″) represent a project-selected nominal search position for interface exploration. The Vela Molecular Ridge is an extended giant molecular cloud complex spanning over 10° x 4° across the galactic plane; it has no single physical centroid.

search_position.search_radius_notes: A 0.05° search radius (~3 arcmin) samples a localized pointing within the complex; full complex coverage requires a mosaic or wide-field catalog query.

VMR_A.name: Vela Cloud A
VMR_A.description: Houses the RCW 38 young embedded cluster with active massive star formation.

VMR_B.name: Vela Cloud B
VMR_B.description: Distant background giant molecular cloud along the line of sight, distinct from the closer A, C, D group.

VMR_C.name: Vela Cloud C
VMR_C.description: Site of active intermediate and massive star formation, including the compact RCW 36 H II region.
VMR_C.reference: Murphy & May (1991) A&A 247, 202; Baba et al. (2004) ApJ 614, 818

VMR_D.name: Vela Cloud D
VMR_D.description: Houses extensive populations of low-to-intermediate mass young stellar objects.
VMR_D.reference: Liseau et al. (1992) A&A 265, 577; Elia et al. (2007) A&A 467, 759

vela-ridge.description: A massive interstellar molecular cloud complex in the southern sky, segmented into Clouds A, B, C, and D. Clouds A, C, and D form a coherent physical group at ~700–1,000 pc, whereas Cloud B is a separate background GMC at ~2,000 pc.

hotspots.name: VMR Cloud C (d ~700 pc)
hotspots.fact: Site of active cluster formation housing the compact RCW 36 H II region.

hotspots.name: VMR Cloud D (d ~700-1000 pc)
hotspots.fact: Contains rich populations of low-to-intermediate mass young stellar objects.

hotspots.name: VMR Cloud B (d ~2000 pc)
hotspots.fact: Distant background molecular cloud at ~2 kpc, not co-distant with Clouds A, C, D.

vela-ridge.source: Murphy & May (1991) A&A 247, 202; Liseau et al. (1992) A&A 265, 577; NASA IRSA
